You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From b339fc6dbb34d685212599f06efdc17029a06b95 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Greg Bowser <topnotcher@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Oct 2013 23:46:25 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] mpc: fix a logic error that prevented pkts from sending

Fixes an issue that begin with 4cf1605299c06df111acf15cf2e94eb2d52cc562,
where the mpc master would not transmit any messages.
---
 include/mpc.c | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/include/mpc.c b/include/mpc.c
index b2fa669..07b32e7 100644
--- a/include/mpc.c
+++ b/include/mpc.c
@@ -358,8 +358,8 @@ static inline void mpc_master_run(void) {
 	ATOMIC_BLOCK(ATOMIC_RESTORESTATE) {
 		if ( queue_empty(&tx_state.queue.hdr) || tx_state.status != TX_STATUS_IDLE ) 
 			okay = 0; 
-
-		tx_state.status = TX_STATUS_BUSY;
+		else 
+			tx_state.status = TX_STATUS_BUSY;
 	}
 	
 	if (!okay) return;
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by a logic error in the conditional statements that determined whether the transmission state should be set to busy. Specifically, the original code did not properly handle the case where the transmission queue was not empty and the status was idle, leading to the status being incorrectly set to busy regardless of the actual conditions. This prevented the master from transmitting any messages, as the status was not being updated correctly based on the queue state. The patch corrects this by ensuring that the status is only set to busy when the queue is not empty and the status is indeed idle.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

    
    Provide a response strictly in the following format:
    Code statements:
    <text1>
    <text2>
    <text3>
    <text4>
    ...
    <textN>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by a logic error in the conditional statements that determined whether the transmission state should be set to busy. Specifically, the original code did not properly handle the case where the transmission queue was not empty and the status was idle, leading to the status being incorrectly set to busy regardless of the actual conditions. This prevented the master from transmitting any messages, as the status was not being updated correctly based on the queue state. The patch corrects this by ensuring that the status is only set to busy when the queue is not empty and the status is indeed idle.
